ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: This study was approved by the University of Pittsburgh Institutional Review Board.
We recruited participants into the Functional neuroanatomy correlates of worry in older adults (FINA) study (R01 MH108509).
They were recruited through a variety of sources including a website resource from the university, recommendations, flyers, and ads.
All participants gave written informed consent prior to participating in the study.
We recruited 131 participants who were ≥ 50 years old, with varying levels of worry severity.
We recruited participants to have a normal distribution on worry severity in the sample as measured by the Penn State Worry Questionnaire (PSWQ) 38 .
table.formatted: We recruited participants to have a normal distribution on worry severity in the sample as measured by the Penn State Worry Questionnaire (PSWQ) <ref type="bibr" target="#b38">38</ref> .

table.text: Participants were excluded if they were diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders, intellectual development disorder, or any form of psychosis or bipolar disorder.
Two participants were tapered off psychotropics.
Participants were in the MR scanner for approximately 45-60 minutes as we also collected functional MRI as well.
Resting state data was acquired over a 6-minute interval while participants were directed to view a white crosshair in the center of a black screen and told to stay awake.

ethics_check.report:
Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, and it was present:

> We recruited participants into the Functional neuroanatomy correlates of worry in older adults (FINA) study (R01 MH108509).

> They were recruited through a variety of sources including a website resource from the university, recommendations, flyers, and ads.

> All participants gave written informed consent prior to participating in the study.

> We recruited 131 participants who were ≥ 50 years old, with varying levels of worry severity.

> We recruited participants to have a normal distribution on worry severity in the sample as measured by the Penn State Worry Questionnaire (PSWQ) 38 .

> Participants were excluded if they were diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders, intellectual development disorder, or any form of psychosis or bipolar disorder.

> Two participants were tapered off psychotropics.

> Participants were in the MR scanner for approximately 45-60 minutes as we also collected functional MRI as well.

> Resting state data was acquired over a 6-minute interval while participants were directed to view a white crosshair in the center of a black screen and told to stay awake.

Ethics approval statement:

> This study was approved by the University of Pittsburgh Institutional Review Board.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

live_data_statements: We recruited participants into the Functional neuroanatomy correlates of worry in older adults (FINA) study (R01 MH108509).
They were recruited through a variety of sources including a website resource from the university, recommendations, flyers, and ads.
All participants gave written informed consent prior to participating in the study.
We recruited 131 participants who were ≥ 50 years old, with varying levels of worry severity.
We recruited participants to have a normal distribution on worry severity in the sample as measured by the Penn State Worry Questionnaire (PSWQ) 38 .
Participants were excluded if they were diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders, intellectual development disorder, or any form of psychosis or bipolar disorder.
